builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Measuring the Energy Cost of Completing Tasks with Quantized Language-Model Agents
summary: The method replaces per-token energy benchmarking of quantized models with per-completed-task measurement across an agent's full run, including tool calls and revisions, as the basis for choosing serving precision. It costs the effort of building pass/fail-checked tasks and measuring CPU and GPU energy per completed run on one's own workload, with no model or infrastructure change required. It can fail if conclusions from published benchmarks are transferred blindly, since whether 4-bit saves energy per task is task-, model-, and budget-dependent.
rationale: The reader can adopt the decision rule directly — compare tokens per completed task against per-token savings when selecting quantization — but must validate it on their own tasks and budget limits before committing a precision to production.
technique: Task-level energy benchmarking for quantized agents

claims.statement: The method replaces per-token energy benchmarking of quantized models with per-completed-task measurement across an agent's full run, including tool calls and revisions, as the basis for choosing serving precision. It costs the effort of building pass/fail-checked tasks and measuring CPU and GPU energy per completed run on one's own workload, with no model or infrastructure change required. It can fail if conclusions from published benchmarks are transferred blindly, since whether 4-bit saves energy per task is task-, model-, and budget-dependent.

4-bit precision generally saves energy per token, but extra tokens to finish a task can make it consume up to 3.5x more energy per completed task than 8-bit, depending on task, model, and execution budget.
